title: Pressure-cooker globe artichokes
subtitle: Tender artichokes in 10 minutes instead of 45
excerpt: Whole globe artichokes steamed under pressure until the leaves pull away easily. The pressure cooker compresses the long steaming time to about 10 minutes and produces artichokes that are ready for dipping straight from the pot.
sourceNotes: Globe artichokes are central to Italian, French, and Spanish cooking and were introduced to England in the 16th century. Steaming whole is the French and Italian home method. The pressure cooker adaptation follows the timing documented in Italian pressure-cooking guides.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Artichokes can be cooked ahead and kept at room temperature for up to 2 hours, or refrigerated for up to 2 days and served cold or at room temperature.

content.text: Globe artichokes are a thoroughly manual eating experience, you pull each leaf, dip the fleshy base in something good, drag it between your teeth, and discard the rest. At the centre is the heart, which is worth the journey. The pressure cooker compresses the usual 40 to 45 minutes of steaming to about 10 minutes and produces artichokes where the leaves pull away cleanly rather than requiring a tug.

Prepare the artichokes by cutting the stem flush, snipping the sharp tip off each outer leaf with scissors, and removing the first two rows of tough outer leaves. A lemon rubbed over the cut surfaces prevents discolouration, artichokes oxidise quickly once cut.
Serve with melted butter, vinaigrette, or aioli for dipping. The artichoke does the work, the dip simply elevates it.

items.prepNote: stems cut flush, leaf tips snipped, outer leaves removed
cut in half, to rub cut surfaces

content.text: Add 300 ml of water to the pressure cooker with the bay leaf and garlic. Place the trivet inside. Rub the cut surfaces of the artichokes with lemon juice, then stand them upright on the trivet, stem down if the stem is trimmed, or on their sides if the stems are removed. Seal the lid and bring to high pressure. Cook at high pressure for 10 to 12 minutes for medium artichokes. Quick-release the pressure.

Test by pulling a leaf from the middle of the artichoke, it should come away easily. If there is resistance, return to pressure for 3 more minutes. Serve immediately with melted butter or vinaigrette for dipping. To remove the choke (the inedible hairy centre), reach the heart by pulling away the inner leaves and scraping out the choke with a spoon.

rows.symptom: The leaves do not pull away easily
rows.cause: The artichokes were very large, or needed more time.
rows.fix: Return to high pressure for 3 minutes. A very large artichoke can take up to 15 minutes.

rows.symptom: The artichokes are discoloured and brown
rows.cause: The cut surfaces were exposed to air without lemon juice, causing oxidation.
rows.fix: This is purely cosmetic. For next time, rub every cut surface with lemon immediately after cutting.

content.text: Globe artichokes arrive in British markets from March. They are a communal eating experience: slow, sociable, and suited to a long starter. The pressure cooker makes them practical on a weeknight.
